Explain photosynthesis in simple terms.

Photosynthesis is the process plants use to convert light energy into chemical energy stored in glucose.

The basic steps are:

  • Sunlight is absorbed by chlorophyll in the leaves
  • Water is taken up by the roots and carbon dioxide from the air
  • These are combined to produce glucose and oxygen
6 CO2 + 6 H2O + light energy -> C6H12O6 + 6 O2
Which part of the cell does this happen in?

Photosynthesis takes place in the chloroplasts, specifically within stacks of membranes called thylakoids, where chlorophyll captures light energy.

The surrounding fluid, the stroma, is where the resulting energy is used to build glucose in the Calvin cycle.
